Comments: VASCULAR NECROSIS AND HEMORRHAGE TONGUE AND FACIAL SOFT TISSUES (RESEMBLING SNAKEBITE). This 18-year-old male southern black rhinoceros has a history of cutaneous melanomas in multiple locations. Recently the animal has had a low white blood cell count but no evidence of illness. The animal was subsequently found dead unexpectedly. A trail of saliva was present in the pen suggesting that the animal regurgitated and paced before falling dead. Necropsy revealed good body condition adequate fat stores marked submandibular swelling hemorrhage in the ventral tongue bloody saliva from the mouth a focus of broken skin at the caudal edge of the lateral digit and one caudal to that on the left front foot severely edematous tissue in the ventral mandible associated with leakage of clear fluid edematous tissue lateral to the epiglottis although the glottis and epiglottis were otherwise normal. Copious amounts of sanguineous thick foam extended down the trachea to the bronchi and into some of the bronchioles. The dependent lung was reddened. The tongue was severely swollen and protruding from the mouth occupying nearly the entire oral cavity and hemorrhage was present on the ventral surface of the tongue. Two slightly raised black masses were in the maxillary gingiva on the left side and some calculus was embedded in the maxillary gingival tissue near the caudal molars. Cysts containing white material were in the thyroids. The duodenal and jejunal mucosa were multifocally reddened. Gastric contents were alfalfa and no other plant material. No other remarkable findings were noted.

OSTEOARTHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC MYOSITIS CYSTIC BILIARY HYPERPLASIA HEP[ATIC FIBROSIS. This 4-year-old female opossum had a previous diagnosis of spindle cell sarcoma. The animal developed ataxia in the rear limb and was humanely euthanized.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE RETINAL MELANOMA. This approximately 3-year-old spayed Virginia opossum developed hind limb weakness and an unsteady gait similar to that of a male opossum that was a sibling. Necropsy revealed small nodules in the subcutis of the chest fat deposits around the eyes heart and abdominal viscera mottled liver and some pink raised nodules in the lungs.

POLIOENCEPHALOMALACIA DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE HYPERTENSION ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS EOSINOPHILIC ENTERITIS ASPIRATION. This 16-year-old male leopard has a three-month history of a sarcoma on the toe and has a one-week history of neurologic disorder with cortical blindness following an anesthetic procedure. The animal was showing some improvement before being found lethargic in the morning deteriorating throughout the day followed by a seizure in the afternoon and cardiac arrest. Necropsy revealed partial dehiscence at the toe amputation site muscle atrophy around the hips and shoulders fractured bottom two canines with exposure of the pulp in the left canine a small amount of digesta in the small intestine some ingesta in the stomach a 1 cm. cyst-like mass in the right hepatic lobe and a 1 mm. black slightly raised mass on the edge of the right hepatic lobe. The right kidney was subjectively larger than the left and had an area of dark discoloration on the serosal surface that extended into the parenchyma. The urinary bladder had five pale to dark red raised cyst-like masses up to 1 cm. in greatest dimension. A small focus of the frontal cortex was paler than the surrounding tissue at about the level of the optic chiasm.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ULCERATIVE STOMATITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 11-year-old spayed female tiger had a prior diagnosis of epitheliotropic T-cell lymphoma. Treatment was initiated; however skin erosions eventually recurred. Recently anorexia anemia and azotemia were diagnosed. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy areas of alopecia were noted. Erosions were present in the oral cavity and esophagus. Hemorrhage was noted in the GI tracts. Lungs were edematous. Kidneys were pale tan and irregular.

ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS REACTIVE SYSTEMIC AMYLOIDOSIS CUTANEOUS ABSCESS. This 22.5-year-old female tiger was diagnosed four years earlier with cutaneous hemangiosarcoma. For the past few months it was noted that this animal was losing weight and was draining from a malodorous mass. Radiographs revealed possible metastasis in the lungs and a possible mass in the caudal abdomen. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cystic ovaries multiple firm masses in both uterine horns multiple small white firm nodules throughout the lungs small kidneys with irregular surfaces and pale parenchyma thick pancreas with multiple firm nodules thick duodenum with multiple firm masses a few enlarged jejunal lymph nodes and irregular slightly friable liver.

VASCULITIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male tiger had a four day period of partial inappetence and abdominal discomfort with progressive unilateral epistaxis on the right side of one month’s duration. Over the past several months the tiger had been observed to be coughing. The tiger has a history of eosinophilic granuloma lymphoma and is currently in remission following chemotherapy. The tiger also has inflammatory bowel disease and chronic renal disease. Endoscopy revealed a small soft tissue mass in the proximal turbinates and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fibrotic kidneys colonic ulceration and intestinal thickening soft palate ulceration a white nodular nasal lesion thickening of the apical aspect of the urinary bladder and a focal raised lesion of the musculature over the cervical spine.

EUTHANASIA RUMENITIS LYMPHADENITIS INANITION. This 3-year/10-month-old male pudu was humanely euthanized. It presented severely hypothermic and hypoglycemic recumbent cold and nonresponsive. Despite supportive care the pudu’s condition did not improve. It also had a chronic history of elevated alkaline phosphatase and globulins. Recent blood work showed elevated AST alkaline phosphatase globulin and phosphorus as well as a hematocrit of 26% and monocytosis of 8%. At necropsy the pudu was moderately thin and dehydrated. There was approximately 200 ml. of serosanguineous fluid within the thoracic and abdominal cavity. Thoracic lymph nodes were prominent. There were several small ovoid firm white masses attached to the mesentery. The spleen was small and whitish-gray. The adrenal glands appeared irregular in shape and texture. The pancreas was pink/brown. Analysis of the thoracic fluid revealed effusion suggestive of intrathoracic lymphosarcoma with a monomorphic population of immature lymphocytes. Sections of heart lung liver kidney lymph node and abdominal mass were frozen for future use if needed.

SEMINOMA. This adult sculpin has a three day history of being upside-down in the tank. The fish appeared lethargic. Examination revealed anchor worms on the body cloudy left eye red gills increased gilling activity and reddening of the pectoral rays. The fish died and necropsy revealed a mottled fatty liver tapeworms in the intestine reduced body fat a 3 cm. mass involving the left reproductive organ and a 0.5 cm. mass involving the right reproductive organ.

EMACIATION. This 5- to 7-year-old female lovebird is from a multiple bird aviary in which the male conspecific died due to complications associated with pulmonary small cell carcinoma. Necropsy revealed no abnormalities.

SHOCK. This approximately 10-year-old female copperhead was found dead in the enclosure. It had a previous squamous cell carcinoma removed from the tail. At necropsy there was a small amount of internal body fat stores. There were two round raised approximately 2 mm. in diameter lesions on the hepatic capsular surface. The gastrointestinal tract was empty except for foaming mucus within the stomach. The proximal small intestine was dilated and dark purple.

CUTANEOUS MELANOMA ATHEROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 14-year-old female copperhead has a history of neoplasia involving the skin and fly-strike is present in the area where the tumor is necrotic. Prior to death the snake had a history of hypercholesterolemia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA COLITIS ENTERITIS INTUSSUSCEPTION BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 10-year-old female howler monkey had a history of partial anorexia and weight loss. An exploratory laparotomy revealed thickening of the cecum and enlargement of the mesenteric lymph nodes. Biopsies revealed lymphoid follicular hyperplasia or possible emerging lymphoma. The animal’s condition continued to decline despite treatment with lethargy and vomiting and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the body was thin to emaciated. An intussusception of the distal small intestine and ileum was identified with marked hemorrhage and friable intestine in the distal portion. The cecum and proximal colon were thickened and had foci of hemorrhage beneath the serosa.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS CHRONIC UVEITIS CATARACT SEMINOMA URATE STASIS. This 16-year-old mal teal had a long-term history of chronic uveitis and blindness. Recently weight loss and lameness were also noted. The animal was humanely euthanized. Radiographically moderate to severe osteoarthritis was noted in the stifles. At necropsy the animal was thin with minimal fat depots and muscle wasting. The left eye was shrunken and scarred. The right eye was opaque with foci of yellow and dark black.
SEMINOMA INANITION. This 4-year-old duck was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a large mass was present in the anterior coelom along the right side. The bird was thin.

SEMINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male Pekin duck has a two week history of anorexia and polydyspnea with mild anemia and slightly high lead level. Radiographs revealed a mass in the cranial dorsal coelom and exploratory surgery revealed a 5 cm. testicular neoplasm that was nonresectable and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

SEMINOMAS. This 13-year-old male duck had cataracts and impaired vision. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed active testicles and the testicles had irregular consistency with firm and hard regions.

\_ Oral cavity: Moderate chronic stomatitis Liver: Mild melanomacrophage hyperplasia Skin: Focal degenerating parasite Comment: A cause of death was not evident; nor was a cause for the most prominent lesion; stomatitis; visible. A source of the seeping white material noted grossly was not identified; but this may have been related to the stomatitis.

1. Liver: Melanomacrophage hyperplasia; mild Comment: Lesions were limited to mild hepatic melanomacrophage hyperplasia. No additional lesions were found on sections examined to explain the cause of death.

Kidney: Severe tubular degeneration and necrosis; crystal formation; and mild chronic glomerulonephritis Liver: Moderate melanomacrophage center hyperplasia Skeletal muscle: Moderate multifocal myofiber degeneration Comment: The most severe lesion and the likely cause of death in this toad was the renal tubular degeneration. This is most likely due to physiologic or toxic damage; and not an infectious cause. Degeneration may also play a role. The liver and skeletal muscle changes may be a result of the renal disease; but are non-specific

\_ Kidney: Severe; acute tubular necrosis Liver: Severe melanomacrophage center hyperplasia Coelomic mesentery: Mild multifocal necrosis Comment: A specific cause of death was not clear; but the renal tubular necrosis suggests a toxic or hypoxic event. Melanomacrophage centers increase in size and number in response to environmental; pathogen; or metabolic stresses - typically over a prolonged period of time. The marked increase in the number and size in this animal suggests there may have been some on-going environmental stress; perhaps with a final decompensation resulting in the renal lesion.

Liver: Vacuolar hepatopathy; diffuse Liver: Hepatic lipidosis; multifocal; mild Liver: Extramedullary hematopoiesis; mild Liver: Melanomacrophage hyperplasia; mild Spleen: Mesothelial hypertrophy Testes: Mesothelial hypertrophy Comment: The main histologic finding was diffuse hydropic change of the liver; consistent with hepatopathy of unknown cause. Hepatic dysfunction may have been the underlying cause of death as well as the coelomic effusion noted grossly. Mesothelial hypertrophy of the spleen and testes was likely secondary to the coelomic effusion. Hepatic extramedullary hematopoiesis is a common; incidental finding. Melanomacrophage hyperplasia was age-related. All tissues were moderately autolyzed. Sarah Corner; DVM; MS; Diplomate ACVP

AMELONITIC MELANOMA. This 10-year-old anole had a limb amputated approximately three months prior to death due to amelanotic melanoma. The animal was found dead. At necropsy masses were present in the lung and pale foci were present in the liver and kidney.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDITIS EPICARDITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS URINARY CALCULI. This 16-year-old otter had a history of testicular seminoma. Hemorrhagic enteritis was noted; however cardiopulmonary arrest developed under anesthesia. At necropsy fat depots were markedly reduced. Organs were pale. The small intestine and cecum contained thick hemorrhagic contents. Renal calculi were noted in the kidneys.

PROVENTRICULAR DILATATION DISEASE SEMINOMA. This 44-year-old male macaw died with no prior signs of illness. The bird was found at the bottom of its cage weak and dyspneic and died at an emergency clinic. The bird had lost 300 gm. since its last routine health check. Necropsy revealed emaciation and distended abdomen. The internal exam revealed a distended proventriculus impacted with undigested seeds and other materials. The carcass appeared to be more autolyzed than expected.

POSTSURGICAL CLOACAL OBSTRUCTION INTRATUBULAR SEMINOMA. This adult male blue and gold macaw is part of the Oregon Humane Society investigation case #13655. The animal had a chronic cloacal prolapse upon admission which was surgically repaired with a purse string suture. One week later the bird was found dead. At necropsy the animal was in thin body condition with alopecia. The purse string suture was still present but the proctodeum was swollen with urates and feces. The liver was mildly congested. There was bilateral scarring along the patagial ligaments causing poor extension of both wings which was noted antemortem as well.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA WITH SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This adult female hedgehog had been examined six months prior to death for anorexia and dental disease. The animal presented with an acute onset of pallor lethargy and agonal breathing and was euthanized. The animal was from an area of the Children’s Zoo where a few small mammals have had mycoplasma pneumonias. A sibling of this animal was euthanized with leukemic lymphosarcoma. Necropsy revealed an absence of internal fat reserves dense lungs that sank in formalin and only scant ingesta and feces present in the alimentary tract.

VACUOLAR DEGENERATION (BRAIN SPINAL CORD). This 5-year-old female hedgehog developed progressive ataxia. Squamous cell carcinoma was diagnosed in the oral cavity. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy irregular pink lesions were noted in the gingiva. Muscle wasting was noted over the hips and spine.

EUTHANASIA ASTROCYTOMA CARDIOMYOPATHY. This approximately 3-year/1-month-old female hedgehog was humanely euthanized. It had acute onset of lameness of the right front limb. Evaluation revealed abnormal caudal extension of the right front limb. The animal responded to pain in the limb but was unable to flex it. Whole body radiographs revealed no abnormalities. The animal’s condition remained unchanged until July 12th at which time it was unable to flex both front limbs and was unable to ambulate eat or drink on its own. Supportive care was given. At necropsy the skin was mildly scaly. There was a 1 cm. long region of midjejunum that was dilated and filled with gas and yellow/green fluid. The spleen was enlarged.

DEGENERATIVE LEUKOENCEPHALOMYELOPATHY CONSISTENT WITH WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME FIBRILLAR ASTROCYTOMA. This captive bred 4-year-old female hedgehog had progressive loss of motor control on the hind limbs over the past year. The hind limbs also appeared dark in color frequently. The animal was euthanized.

EUTHANASIA WHITE MATTER VACUOLIZATION PITUITARY ENLARGEMENT ENTERITIS ASTROCYTOMA. This 3.5-year-old male hedgehog presented with central blindness and dilated pupils. Ocular lesions were not identified. The animal was ataxic and was euthanized.

WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME ASTROCYTOMA CHRONIC UROCYSTITIS WITH SEPSIS PAPILLARY NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 1-year-old male hedgehog had a history of intermittent and mild leaning to the right which progressed to weakness ataxia and dull mentation loss of appetite and weight loss. The animal did not respond to a five day trial of meloxicam and omega-3. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

GEMISTOCYTIC ASTROCYTOMA HIPPOCAMUPS; NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION WITH SPONGIFORM CHANGE BRAIN AND SPINAL CORD DEGENERATIVE DISC DISEASE AND VERTEBRAL DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS. This 3-year-old female/spayed hedgehog has a history of paresis of eight months duration and died suddenly. Necropsy revealed a small tear in the right ventricle of the heart large thyroid and adrenals and no other abnormalities.

ASTROCYTOMA DEGENERATIVE DISK DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old hedgehog was found in its exhibit holding facility on its side and unable to move its hind legs. The animal was bright and alert but with significant bilateral hind limb paresis but could retract its hind limbs in an attempt to roll into a ball. Deep pain was also present in both limbs. The animal did not respond to several days of dexamethasone treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA ABSCESS AXONOPATHY CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY. This approximately 5-year-old female hedgehog was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic hematuria that responded to antibiotics. It had multiple abdominal masses on ultrasound and exploratory laparotomy revealed an enlarged uterus and left ovary. Histologic diagnosis was an ovarian carcinoma and uterine adenocarcinoma. At necropsy the kidneys were cystic. The liver appeared congested. There was a mass/abscess within the caudal abdomen that was associated with the gastrointestinal tract. Postoperatively this hedgehog developed posterior paresis and was slow to return to normal.

LEUKOENCEPHALOMYELOPATHY (WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME) DEGENERATIVE DISC. This 4-year-old male/intact hedgehog was diagnosed with an osteosarcoma of the right femur necessitating amputation and hemipelvectomy in October 2015. Narrow margins were obtained at surgery. In April the animal developed an onset of nonambulatory tetraparesis with weight loss inappetence neurologic signs and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed emaciation a firm yellow subcutaneous mass at the previous surgical site bilateral ureteral dilatation pelvic dilatation and displaced right testicle. A 2 mm. mass of bony consistency was attached to the ventral vertebral bodies at the thoracolumbar junction and a 7 mm. yellow hard mass was attached to the periosteum of the ventral aspect of the right ischium. A 1 cm. white spherical mass was in the splenic mesentery and the spleen was covered in small raised masses with splenic-like parenchyma. Multiple 2 mm. spherical white nodules were on the peritoneal surface of the left diaphragmatic crus.

ASTROCYTOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. This 5-year-old hedgehog had a history of progressive ataxia weakness inappetence and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mature cataract in the right eye and early cataract in the left eye. Some mild bruising was in the ventral cervical area (venipuncture site) adipose stores were abundant two round symmetrical masses were on either side of the trachea in the ventral midcervical region. The masses were beige and homogeneous. Thyroid glands were subjectively enlarged and pale tan. The left pleural cavity was filled with cloudy fluid and the left lung was diffusely dark red and consolidated. The right pleural cavity contained a large blood clot (intracardiac euthanasia). The right lung was diffusely dark red and consolidated. The heart was subjectively enlarged and the left ventricle was subjectively thickened. The liver was diffusely pale brown. The stomach contained feed material and the intestines were basically empty. The kidneys were diffusely pale and the right kidney contained a large fluid-filled cyst in the cranial pole.

GASTRIC BLOAT ATHEROSCLEROSIS ENTEROCOLITIS WITH CILIATED PROTOZOA. This 29-year-old male spider monkey was diagnosed with presumptive lymphoma and died unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed edema and fibrin tags over the abdomen and thorax moderate perilaryngeal edema severe gastric distention with food (mainly lettuce) thin walled stomach and gas distended intestinal tract with petechiae in the small intestine. Lymph nodes were numerous and all were enlarged. The spleen was small rounded and congested. The liver had mottling with congestion and pallor. Air bubbles were under the capsules of the kidneys and both poles of the kidneys had a bruised or stippled appearance on the surface with associated perirenal edema. The adrenals were enlarged and yellowish. The pericardial sac was adhered to the heart in three spots near the apex. Rough areas of the mucosa were noted in the aorta. Numerous pinpoint black dots were in the lungs.

FACIAL MELANOMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old captive bred fer-de-lance was identified with an approximately 8 cm. irregular circular lesion on the right cheek with multiple small granular spheres resembling a papilloma. The right pupil was much smaller than the left. Severe vertebral fusion and spondylitic proliferation was in the caudal third of the spinal column and one large region of lordosis was noted. The right quadrate bone of the skull was fractured and deviated laterally. The caudal aspect of the cranial fragment was bulbus and osteolytic. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed yellow fluid in the coelom thickened atrioventricular valves gross thickening and irregularities to the caudal third of the vertebral column a firm callus at the junction of the right quadrate bone fracture and no other gross abnormalities.

BACTERIAL OSTEOARTHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This adult male pitviper was noted to be inappetent and had dorsal spinal swelling two months prior to death. A previous mass was surgically excised and diagnosed as a fibrosarcoma. Radiographs of the spinal mass were consistent with a fracture. The swelling continued to increase with two additional enlargements noted cranial to the original swelling. Supportive care was administered but the snake lost function of the distal body and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and a 1 cm. in diameter spherical swelling in the dorsal spinal region approximately two-thirds distal from the head. The ventral aspect of the lesion ventral to the vertebra consisted entirely of friable caseous material. Two smaller firm swellings 0.3 cm. in diameter were present approximately 2 cm. proximal to the original mass. Only the dorsal spinal column appeared to be involved in these specimens.

ATHEROSCLEROSIS VISCERAL GOUT BEAK NECROSIS. This approximately 33-year-old wild caught male hornbill died. It had a history of squamous cell carcinoma on the beak that was treated. It also had a history of depression and listlessness following its last surgery. At necropsy there was severe gout. There were deposits of urates on the serosal surfaces of coelomic viscera. The pericardium and coelomic membranes were completely covered in white deposits. There was severe zonal myositis. There was a large 4 cm. area of subcutaneous emphysema and hemorrhage in the mid pectoral region. The entire upper rostrum had been removed from surgery and excision. The remaining tissues showed no signs of recurrence of the squamous cell carcinoma. The right iris was discolored.

CHRONIC CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 35-year-old female captive bred cockatoo had a 2.5 year history of illness and was euthanized. The bird had a history of undifferentiated sarcoma (G98-1902 G97-1331) involving the wing. No additional information is provided (necropsy report to follow).

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male squirrel had a history of cutaneous amelanotic melanoma which was removed in August. The animal recently developed vomiting and was euthanized due to poor prognosis. At necropsy no evidence of tumor regrowth was noted. The stomach had an area of hyperemia along the greater curvature.

INTERVERTEBRAL DISC DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SEMINOMA PERIVASCULAR AND PERIBRONCHIOLAR PULMONARY CUFFS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old male coyote had a four-month history of illness and had lost a substantial amount of muscle mass especially in the hind limbs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed decreased range of motion in the lumbar vertebrae compression of the spinal cord at T13-L1 spondylosis slightly mottled liver severe degenerative joint disease in the shoulders mild vegetative lesions in the mitral valves empty stomach esophagus and small intestine and normal feces in the colon.

INTRATHORACIC MESOTHELIOMA. This 6-year-old female wolf was introduced to another female on 11/16 and was started on antibiotics on 11/17 for multiple bite wounds that did not appear to be life-threatening. Keepers had noted recent weight gain and the animal appeared to be adjusting well to its cagemate. The animal developed a one day history of dyspnea and was found dead. Necropsy revealed bloated abdomen containing straw colored to serosanguineous fluid large mesenteric lymph nodes enlarged mediastinal lymph node pulmonary atelectasis small hard white foci in the lung fields bloody fluid in the pericardial sac with marked pericardial thickening and multiple raised nodular foci on the pericardial surface. The liver was firm with rounded edges and areas of tan discoloration. The omentum was icteric and emboli were seen in the mesentery.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PUMONARY EDEMA INSULINOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 15-year-old female jackal was found comatose. Treatment was initiated; however cardiopulmonary arrest ensued. At necropsy the animal was obese. Several lipomas were noted in the skin. The liver was enlarged friable and mottled. Kidneys were small and irregular. Pale tan streaks were present in the cortex.

MESOTHELIOMA. This 12-year-old goat had a recent episode of dyspnea and hyperthermia following a hoof trim. The animal was found dead a few days later. At gross necropsy the abdominal cavity contained a large amount of cloudy fluid with white flocculent material. There were also numerous slightly raised masses on the omentum and severe serous atrophy of all adipose tissue.

HYDRONEPHROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS URETERAL CALCULI CYSTITIS INSULINOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ADRENALITIS. This 9-year-old female guinea pig underwent surgery to remove bladder stones. The animal recovered; however posterior paresis developed two weeks later. At necropsy erosions were noted on the plantar surface of the feet. Pinpoint brown foci were noted in the lungs. Ureters were dilated and contained calculi. Kidneys showed dilation of the renal pelvises with calculi.

HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS LYMPHOPLASMACYTIC ENTERITIS. This 1.5-year-old male guinea pig developed a chondrosarcoma in the hind leg requiring amputation. The cavy died four days after the surgical procedure. Necropsy revealed congested lungs markedly enlarged friable and yellow liver and gas in the stomach and small intestine.

SEPSIS PULMONARY ABSCESS. This 4-year-old male guinea pig had a mammary gland adenocarcinoma removed in February 2013. The animal had been clinically stable since other than mild nasal discharge of several days duration. The animal died unexpectedly and necropsy revealed a small discolored slightly raised area in the caudal hepatic lobe numerous brown spots in the lungs a small amount of clear pericardial fluid enlarged left submandibular lymph node and normal ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract.

INTESTINAL AND COLONIC INTUSSUSCEPTIONS SPLENIC HEMATOMA LIMBIC MELANOMA. This 10-year-old male Patagonian cavy was a little off in the morning and found dead in the afternoon in rigor and bloated. Necropsy revealed a distended abdomen good body condition 200 ml. of hemorrhagic fluid in the peritoneal cavity tan/yellow liver a 1 cm. firm mass at the head of the spleen that was mottled black and white on cut surface bilaterally symmetrical large adrenals a 15-20 cm. intussusception of the jejunum with associated hemorrhage on the serosa a possible intussusception at the ileocecocolic junction with associated hemorrhage in the caecal serosa and approximately 4 cm. of ileum incarcerated inside the cecum although easily reducible. Small infarcts of both kidneys were noted.

STRESS MYOCARDIAL NECROSIS SEMINOMA POSSIBLE ANT BITE ENVENOMATION. This 3-year-old male veiled chameleon had recently become weak in the back legs and had an inability to climb and appears to have received bite wounds from crickets. Necropsy revealed thin body condition multiple small bite wounds on the tail and no other gross abnormalities.

MELANOMA PAPILLOMA EUTHANASIA. This adult female shark has a history of skin lesions along the dorsal back. The lesions were nodular and coalescing gray/black scar-like lesions that slowly progressed over the last year and appear similar to previously diagnosed papillomatous skin disease in cohorts. The shark also had multiple areas of normal appearing skin that was completely pigmented black. In some of these areas there were thickened raised smooth nodules up to 3 cm. in greatest dimension scattered over the body in areas without black pigmentation as well. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and necropsy did not identify visceral nodules.

DYSGERMINOMA EUTHANASIA GASTRITIS HYDRONEPHROSIS. This 8-year-old female maned wolf had a large discrete dysgerminoma removed from the abdomen in August 2009 (G09-4088). Regular growth of tumor was noted over the last year especially on the dorsal lower abdomen. The animal responded and acted normal until two weeks ago. Necropsy revealed massive bilateral tumor in the lower abdomen cystic ovaries enlarged vacuolated uterus with thin wall and enlarged mammary glands with secretory material. The left kidney was small and the right kidney was enlarged. Only the right ureter was found.

EUTHANASIA OVARIAN DYSGERMINOMA BILIARY HYPERPLASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTERIAL AMYLOIDOSIS AORTIC MINERALIZATION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS. This 15-year-old female maned wolf had a history of weight loss and possible seizures. On physical exam a large mass was present in the mid abdomen. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large mass was present effacing the right ovary. The mass measured 15 x 8 x 10 cm. and contained multiple small cystic foci. The liver also contained numerous 0.5-1.5 cm. in diameter cystic foci. A tubular cartilaginous 25 x 7 mm. piece of tissue was identified at the thoracic inlet adjacent to the trachea.

CATARACT RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMA SEMINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old pheasant had been retired to an indoor heated bird aviary due to its age and vision impairment 1.5 years earlier. It subsequently presented with head bobbing behavior and appeared to be blind. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. No gross lesions were identified other than bilateral cataracts and the bird was in good nutritional status.

DEGENERATIVE JOIN DISEASE CATARACT SEMINOMAS AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male quail was euthanized due to age-related degenerative processes that included cataracts poor plumage and loose stools. Necropsy revealed a friable liver and no other abnormalities.

SEMINOMA TRAUMA. This 5-year-old male roller had a one day history of paresis. The bird was administered supportive therapy but died. Necropsy revealed cervical bruising and gas distended gastrointestinal tract. This bird is from an aviary with confirmed avian tuberculosis.

EUTHANASIA CHOLESTEROL GRANULOMA EPICARDIAL FIBROSIS HEMATOMA. This 20-year-old male tree boa had a history of neurologic signs for the past five years. A kidney was removed approximately one year prior to death due to adrenal adenocarcinoma. The animal was found on the floor of the exhibit and did not respond to external stimuli. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a small dark purple mass was identified anterior to the splenopancreas. Approximately 8 cc. of serosanguineous fluid was present within the caudal coelomic cavity.

SEPTICEMIA. This approximately 14-year-old female boa was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic anorexia. It had been force fed since last October. It had both an adenocarcinoma associated with the bowel wall and a granuloma removed. It had colonic atony dilatation and gas distention. At necropsy there was a large hemorrhagic unorganized mass in the fat just cranial to the vent and dorsal to the colon. The mass felt firm but rubbery and had a lacy appearance. The mass was approximately 4-5 cm. in length and 1-2 cm. in diameter. The fat it was contained in was necrotic. There was also a very large amount of gas in the coelomic cavity entrapped around the fat in the caudal third of the body. The gas was accompanied with approximately 30 ml. of brown translucent fluid. There were very little fat deposits in the rest of the body. There was a small oval mass that was flat and dark red and firmly adhered to the body wall about 20 cm. cranial to the vent. It had a smooth surface and may have actually been outside of the coelomic cavity. There was a well organized encapsulated mass in the coelomic fat approximately 25 cm. cranial to the vent. The mass was surrounded by a few ml. of turgid salmon colored fluid. The mass had rounded borders a smooth surface dark red to purple and was homogeneous on cross section. The pericardial sac was thickened. There was an unorganized mass that conformed to the shape of the heart and pericardium within the pericardial sac. The epicardial surface was thickened gray and edematous.

EPIDERMAL NECROSIS (VENTRAL DISTRIBUTION) RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS SEPSIS MELANOMACROPHAGE INCLUSIONS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This adult frog was found dead on exhibit with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed good body condition some hyperkeratosis on the midventral skin mild thickening of the medial aspect of the hind limbs mild erythema on the ventral skin a small white lesion in the left hepatic lobe active female reproductive tract and congestion of several ovarian follicles in the left ovary.

SEMINOMAS RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT EMACIATION. This 2-year-old parakeet has a few week history of decreased appetite and distended coelom. The bird died and necropsy revealed yellow fluid in the coelomic cavity and a 3 cm. firm tan mass in the coelom originating on the left side near the adrenal/gonad/kidney or spleen. Some flat pale irregular lesions were in the liver and the carcass was emaciated.

SEMINOMA. This 5- to 10-year-old female (presumed by curator) captive bred koi died spontaneously and was refrigerated four hours prior to necropsy. The koi was found dead in the duck pond with no previous history of illness. Necropsy revealed pinkish areas around the gill and tail. A mass of pink/gray tissue was adhered to and surrounding the gastrointestinal tract. The liver appeared small and cranially displaced by the abdominal mass.

MESOTHELIOMA. This 15-year-old female fallow deer was found dead. At necropsy the thoracic cavity contained 5 liters of clear yellow to orange fluid. A white mass approximately 12 cm. in diameter was present in the ventral thoracic cavity. The mass was cavitated with a central necrotic area containing purulent material. The pleura and pericardium had numerous white nodules ranging from 5 mm. to 3 cm. Similar nodules were present throughout the lungs.

MELANOMA EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male fallow deer had a melanoma removed from the left medial canthus in October 2011. The deer developed a firm subcutaneous mass near the jaw on February 16 2012. Supportive care was administered but the mass was larger at the time of second treatment and the animal’s quality of life was poor with thin body condition a decreased appetite and unthrifty haircoat. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition scant fat stores a 10 cm. subcutaneous mass in the left jaw region extending deep into underlying connective tissues. The mass was dark black on cut surface and closely adhered to the ramus. Enlarged and dark retropharyngeal mandibular lymph nodes were noted and the mass appeared to extend into the left jugular vein. Multiple dark firm nodules up to 4 cm. in diameter were present in the lungs and the lungs were congested and edematous. Abomasal mucosa was hyperemic with areas resembling erosions.

CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE. This approximately 12-year-old male agouti went into respiratory arrest and despite efforts to revive it died. It had been doing well since its arrival in 1999. It was housed with a female that died of bronchoalveolar carcinoma. This animal was moved to a new enclosure two weeks ago and seemed to be doing well. It was found the day of death on its side in extensor rigidity and gasping for breath. At necropsy there was blood coming out of the nostrils and copious amounts of foamy material in the oral cavity. The muscles were congested. The kidneys were swollen and grainy on the capsular surface. The pulmonary airways contained hemorrhage. The lungs had the appearance of hyperinflation. The heart was globoid and cardiac vessels were injected. There were some plaques on the leaflets of the mitral valve. There was a normal penis but no testis could be found. A structure shaped similar to a uterus but without the musculature was discovered dorsal to the bladder. The brain had some petechia.

EUTHANASIA SEMINOMA ENTERITIS. This 14-year-old male whistling duck had a history of stumbling and ataxia. The animal’s condition declined and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a 7 x 5 cm. soft tissue mass was present in the coelomic cavity (possible testis). Other organs had no significant gross lesions.

SEMINOMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male duck has a history of lameness ataxia and elevated uric acid levels. The bird was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed bilateral multilobular cystic structures in the testes. The heart was enlarged and the epicardium had an irregular surface.

SEMINOMA CEREBELLAR MICROGRANULOMAS (RESEMBLING TREMATODE EGGS) EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male whistling duck presented for acute lameness and incoordination. Examination revealed ataxia and stumbling or falling over when attempting to step. Blood work was within normal limits. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition good feather condition a pinion in the right wing corneal opacity in the left eye pale liver pale kidneys and a firm mottle highly vascular 6 cm. space-occupying mass in the left cranial dorsal coelomic cavity.

RENAL GOUT INANITION GASTRITIS. This 21-year-old female snake had a prior history of a liposarcoma which was surgically removed. Recently there has been a history of poor shedding and retained spectacles. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the body was in poor condition with marked muscle atrophy. Both eyes had retained spectacles. Kidneys were congested and contained large quantities of urates. A caudal coelomic fat body was reddish-brown on sectioning and was highly vascular.

COLITIS WITH IMPLANTED BONE ENDOCARDIAL THROMBOSIS WITH PAPILLARY INFARCT MELANOMA. This adult male speckled racer is a long-time zoo resident that had refused its last three feedings and had a bloody discharge from the cloaca. A 6 mm. firm mass was on the dorsum 10 cm. behind the head. Radiographs showed a mass effect ventral and cranial to the heart and the snake died that day. Necropsy revealed edema around the heart and kidneys and intramural hemorrhage at the cloaca. The liver was pale and friable.

SEMINOMA INANITION PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 7-year-old male pigeon has a history of marked weight loss. The animal was found dead. At necropsy a 2 cm. in diameter mass was present near the anterior lobe of the left kidney.

PROLAPSED HEMIPENE. This 15-year-old male rat snake had a renal adenocarcinoma two years prior to death. A prolapsed hemipene was removed on 4/23/98. A biopsy of this hemipene was submitted on 5/6 (as stated). Subsequently the snake died on 5/5. Necropsy revealed no abnormalities in the cloacal region to account for the prolapse. All tissues were autolyzed.

SEMINOMA HEPATITIS. This 6-year-old male lory was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy areas of feather loss were noted over the pectoral region and legs (feather picking). Moderate atrophy of the pectoral muscles was also present. A large white lobulated mass was present in the coelomic cavity.

CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS GERIATRIC EUTHANASIA. This 25-yeary-old female zebra had a previous history of two different sarcomas (from 2007 and 2012) and had chronic loss of body condition. Physical examination revealed a left heart systolic murmur and blood work revealed anemia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed dull fur (did not molt for the past two years) pale mucous membranes scars from previous surgeries on the right neck and right axilla a small nodule at the previous incision site of the right axilla (1 cm. in greatest dimension) a fibrotic nodule in the right scapular/humeral area not involving the muscular structures a large subcutaneous hematoma in the neck at a site of catheter placement globoid enlarged heart a moderate amount of clear pericardial fluid enlarged retropharyngeal lymph nodes a 1.5 cm. nodule in the left lung a moderate amount of clear fluid in the thoracic cavity malocclusion with overgrowth in the lingual aspects of the lower jaw teeth loose molars pockets of food between the 5th and 6th molars and between the 4th and 5th molars in the upper right maxillary arcade multiple small areas of congestion in the stomach congestion in the duodenum and jejunum and in the colon reddened and edematous pancreas bilaterally enlarged adrenal glands and no other gross abnormalities.

TRAUMA (CERVICAL LUXATION) INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS ENDARTERITIS CUTANOUS SPINDLE CELL TUMOR IRIS MELANOMA. This approximately 12-year-old male zebra died shortly after arrival after throwing itself into walls. Necropsy revealed good body condition bot larvae in the margo plicatus large and small strongyles throughout the small intestine and severe bruising in the area of C1-C3 with associated subluxation of C1-C2.

XANTHOMATOSIS DYSGERMINOMA BACTERIAL ABSCESS. This 13-year-old female gecko had a history of lethargy and weight loss and a mass was identified by ultrasound. Cytologic examination identified a neoplasm. Multiple masses were removed surgically and gout was noted during the surgical procedure. The animal subsequently died and necropsy revealed thin body condition white gritty material along ventral coelomic veins extending to the hepatic lobes and effacing approximately 50% of the lungs. Inspissated follicles were in the reproductive tract. The stomach contained cricket parts and the colon was moderately distended with fluid and ingesta. Adipose stores were atrophic.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS CATARACTS EUTHANASIA. This 27-year-old male penguin had been on long-term pain management for severe chronic osteoarthritis in the coxofemoral and stifle joints causing markedly decreased mobility. This bird had a partial digital amputation due to digital melanoma in May 2008. This animal’s condition progressively worsened and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified thin body condition bilateral cataracts previously amputated portion of right digit #4 normal ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract testicular asymmetry with the left 1.5x larger than the right osteophyte accumulation and thickening of the joint capsule of the stifle and coxofemoral joints and no other abnormalities.
TRAUMA SEMINOMA VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS. This 20-year-old male bishop was found dead. At necropsy the left testicle was markedly enlarged.

CIRRHOSIS HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMA IRIS MELANOMA CATARACTS ATHEROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 24-year-old female gyrfalcon had an intermittent history of lethargy and inappetence and weakness while flying. Radiographs revealed a large soft tissue opacity in the coelom and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy a large amount of clear yellow/orange fluid was present throughout the coelomic cavity air sacs were cloudy the liver was dark multilobular with multiple firm areas and areas of necrosis and liquefaction. The spleen was pale and the heart was subjectively enlarged. Ovarian material was small and inactive. Lungs were bright red. Bilateral cataracts were noted.

BILATERAL SEMINOMAS EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old male kestrel had experienced a voice change and weight loss over a four-month period. The animal was believed to have a coelomic mass and increased opacity in the left humerus. Aspergillus panels were negative. The mass effect radiographically has enlarged over time and was palpable. During exploratory surgery the mass was considered nonresectable and euthanasia was performed. Necropsy revealed that the mass was white vascular and friable and left a concave section of the left kidney when excised. A similar mass or enlarged testicle was on the right side. A large amount of subcutaneous and cavity fat was noted although the keel muscle was atrophied. Firm green debris was in the lumen of the left humerus.

ACUTE SHOCK SEMINOMA PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS WITH POSSIBLE CRYPTOSPORIDIA. This 6.5-year-old male junglefowl died a few minutes after being released into an exhibit following oral fenbendazole administration. Necropsy reveal a baseball-sized brown/purple mass found in the region of the left testicle. A walnut-sized similar mass was seen in this area as well. Masses were predominantly firm but also contained cavities of soft whitish necrotic tissue on cut surface.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS BILATERAL SEMINOMAS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old male banded rail previously fractured its femur in 2006. It developed lameness in 2012 with some bone proliferation attributed to degenerative osteoarthritis. Supportive care was administered until the bird’s quality of life deteriorated and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed bone proliferation at the previous fracture site fair body condition and a moderate amount of dark-colored fibrinonecrotic debris within the right stifle. Proliferative changes were noted in both stifle joints and tarsi. The great vessels were firm food was in the ventriculus both testes were enlarged and a core of debris was in the right testis.
COELOMIC MELANOMA PROBABLE OVARIAN ORIGIN. This 7-year-old female chicken died. Necropsy revealed purulent material in the coelomic cavity and diffusely necrotic gastrointestinal tract.

SEMINOMA EMACIATION OSTEOARTHRITIS NECROULCERATIVE DERMATITIS PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 10-year-old male white leghorn chicken has a history of losing weight and falling over. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the air sacs were thickened. There was some yellow discoloration of the left pulmonary lobe. The right testis was slightly larger than the left. There was a synovial cyst adjacent to the left metatarsus.

EUTHANASIA BILIARY CYSTS ENTERITIS COELOMITIS URATE STASIS. This 27-year-old nurse shark developed anorexia and lethargy and has been treated for the past five months with antibiotics. Lobulated masses were identified on ultrasound exam adjacent to the liver. A dark skin lesion was diagnosed on biopsy as a melanoma. The animal was anesthetized for laparoscopy and exploratory surgery and was euthanized under anesthesia. At necropsy multiple firm pale or lightly pigmented skin lesions were identified over the body and fins. The liver was enlarged and contained lobular masses on the dorsal aspect ranging from 0.5 to 10 cm. in diameter. The kidney contained a 2 cm. diameter tan/white area. A duct-like structure was identified in the mesentery of the GI tract.

Coelomic cavity: Mesothelial proliferation with yolk aggregates (suggestive of yolk coelomitis) Liver: Moderate melanomacrophage center hyperplasia Comments The histologic findings were most consistent with a florid mesothelial proliferation within the coelomic cavity and covering the surface of multiple coelomic organs. The presence of yolk associated with the areas of mesothelial proliferation was suggestive of an underlying yolk coelomitis. Yolk coelomitis is a well-recognized problem and a significant cause of death in captive adult female lizards; particularly Fiji Island Iguanas (see Stacy et al; J Zoo Wildl Med. 2008 Jun;39(2):161-9.Yolk coelomitis in Fiji Island banded iguanas (Brachylophus fasciatus).The proliferative mesothelial cell population was considered to be a reactive response to free intracoelomic yolk based on the signalment (mature female). The basis for the florid mesothelial response is not known; however it is thought to be influenced by the volume of yolk present ant the chronicity of coelomitis. Jennifer Lamoureux; D
