COCCIDIODOMYCOSIS. This 16-year-old male Malayan sun bear has a four week history of inappetence and lethargy with intermittent cough facial swelling and nasal discharge. Supportive care was administered but the condition worsened and radiographic signs of pneumonia and pulmonary infiltrates were noted. The bear recovered from anesthesia but died overnight. Necropsy revealed pneumonia a hematoma in the tongue cervical hemorrhage and pulmonary hemorrhage. This bear has a history of recurrent squamous cell carcinoma on the lower lip but no current gross lesions in this regard.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA CHRONIC GINGIVITIS DIC GASTRIC AIR EMBOLI EUTHANASIA. This 28-year-old female sun bear has a 10-year history of oral squamous cell carcinoma associated with herpesvirus infection. The condition has been mostly in remission at rechecks. The animal had been treated with various anti-inflammatories and painkillers for arthritis and antibiotics for dental disease. One month earlier the animal had an episode of inappetence with loose stools and became lethargic with slightly elevated respiratory effort. The bear’s condition gradually deteriorated and radiographs revealed extensively consolidated pulmonary fields. Brown flocculent foul-smelling fluid was on the endotracheal tube. Endoscopic exam of the trachea revealed brown fluid at the tracheal bifurcation of the left lung. The animal did not fully recover from anesthesia and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed severe arthritis in the hips approximately 200 ml. of brown foul-smelling fluid in a bulla of the left middle pulmonary lobe and approximately two-thirds of the remaining lungs also affected. Severe chronic dental disease was also noted. The pylorus appeared inflamed. A cataract was also noted.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE OBESITY NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 30-year-old female sun bear had a history of chronic progressive decline in mobility forelimb lameness and did not respond to supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good to excessive nutritional condition mild subcutaneous emphysema around the scapula and lateral to the cranial thorax several small scars on the nasal planum and left oral commissure (previously resected squamous cell carcinomas) a small amount of brown-tinged fluid throughout the right sinus cavity 100 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in each pleural space a small amount of serous pericardial effusion thin right ventricular wall severely advanced osteoarthritic changes in the left elbow with cartilage erosion and many osteophytes. The joint was unstable and bone anatomy was distorted particularly the junction of the ulnar and humeral regions. The left shoulder had moderate erosive osteoarthritis. The right elbow had advanced osteoarthritis but less than the left. Cartilage erosion and osteophytes were noted but the joint was more stable. The right should had severe osteoarthritic changes with cartilage erosions osteophytes and irregular articular surfaces. The stifle joints had moderate erosion of articular cartilage. This bear had a history of oral squamous cell carcinoma and a resected mammary gland adenocarcinoma with no evidence of local recurrence regarding either of the lesions and no evidence of metastases.

DISSEMINATED INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS BACTERIAL OR YEAST. This greater than 30-year-old female Gila monster was diagnosed in 2002 with chronic lymphocytic leukemia and had been under treatment for weight loss and general decline. The lizard died and necropsy revealed approximately 100 cc. of flocculent brown/yellow colored fluid that was malodorous in the coelomic cavity. Active folliculogenesis and adhesions of the reproductive tract to related soft tissues and body wall were also noted.

EUTHANASIA SEMINOMA ARTHRITIS. This 15-year/10-month-old male lechwe was humanely euthanized. It had a history of not doing right weight loss and lameness. At necropsy its body condition was 1. The hip joint surfaces appeared roughened. The animal was extremely thin with no fat present. The bladder was empty. There were possible worm-like raised lesions in the small intestine.

EUTHANASIA HEMATOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS RENAL GOUT HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS INANITION. This 15-year-old male kingsnake had a previous history of renal adenocarcinoma. Recently the animal has lost weight and begun regurgitating. Masses were noted consistent with a hematoma. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy minimal body fat was identified. A 2 x 3 cm. in diameter mass was present near the splenopancreas and a smaller mass was adjacent to the pancreas. The kidney contained gouty deposits.

EUTHANASIA SEMINOMA. This adult male perch was humanely euthanized due to chronic coelomic distention. Two diagnostic cytologic aspirates radiographs and ultrasound suggested neoplastic disease. At necropsy an approximately 1 lb. white multilobulated mass was in the coelomic cavity. On cut section the mass oozed white creamy fluid. Several areas were cystic and several areas were cavitated. The gall bladder was distended with thin yellow/brown bile. There were several 2-3 mm. white nodules on the serosa of the intestine and within the coelomic cavity. The cranial kidney oozed white fluid on cut section and the caudal kidney was highly pigmented.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE AMYLOIDOSIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY HEPATIC NECROSIS. This 16-year-old male ocelot died. It was previously diagnosed with an oral fibrosarcoma in conjunction with azotemia (chronic renal failure). The ocelot’s clinical signs worsened in severity recently. At necropsy the kidneys were firm and fibrotic with irregular margins. The gall bladder was difficult to express. The pancreas appeared inflamed adjacent to the proximal duodenum. The duodenum was thickened proximally. There was diffuse yellow stained abdominal fat.

PROBABLE FIP EUTHANASIA. This 11-month-old intact male serval has a four month history of illness that included constipation cavitary ascites depressed mentation and diarrhea. The cat initially responded to treatment but the condition would return when treatment was discontinued. The cat has tested negative by PCR and antibody titer to feline infectious peritonitis and has also tested negative for feline immunodeficiency virus and feline leukemia virus. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and in addition to the ascites numerous coalescing white nodules were in the kidneys.

SEMINOMA. This greater than 15-year-old smoky jungle frog was hospitalized for supportive care due to emaciated condition but was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and a 3 cm. pale firm yellow mass in the coelomic cavity adjacent to the pancreas. Adhesions of the mass to the gastrointestinal tract were noted.

SEMINOMA INANITION ANTHRACOSIS. This adult male pigeon was found dead on exhibit. The keepers reported seeing this pigeon fluffed at the PM check the day prior to death. At necropsy there was a large defect within the left body wall. The head and neck appeared chewed on by a predator. Some internal organs were missing. The left lung was absent and the right lung was dark and friable. The thoracic air sacs had white foci. The liver was mostly missing and the remaining tissue was dark. The kidneys were uniformly pale and mottled. The left testis was three times larger than the right testis and was creamy white colored. On the serosal surface there were multiple purplish foci and a large central discolored region on the cut surface. The gastrointestinal tract was filled with light tan ingesta and gas.
HEPATIC MELANOMACROPHAGE HYPERPLASIA. This 5-year-old golden mantella was found dead on February 8 2011. Gross necropsy revealed no significant lesions.

HEPATOXINS SEMINOMA. This 10-year-old male turkey had a history of lameness and ataxia that did not respond to treatment. Euthanasia was performed for humane reasons. Necropsy revealed a prominent keel with pressure sores possible abscesses in the liver pale spleen and erosions on the articular surfaces of the stifles with associated thickening of the joint capsules.

SEMINOMA. This adult male budgerigar exhibited weight loss and regurgitation. Gross necropsy revealed dissimilar testes and a thickened right hepatic lobe. The bird is from a home with a history of proventricular dilatation disease.

MACRORHABDIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 6-year-old budgerigar had a high grade poorly differentiated sarcoma on the right leg. The lesion was nonresectable and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. No external or gross abnormalities were noted at necropsy other than the leg tumor.

SEMINOMA MACRORHABDIOSIS EMACIATION. This 9-year-old male budgerigar has a one month history of increased respiratory rate higher than normal body weight sharp keel and a possible mass effect. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a tumor in the liver.

SEMINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old budgerigar of undetermined gender presented one month earlier with increased respiratory rate and received supportive care. On day #7 of treatment the bird was accidentally released from its cage into the aviary and treatment at that time was discontinued. The bird subsequently represented with tachypnea and inability to fly and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed slight overconditioning reddened gastrointestinal tract abnormally small and empty proventriculus normal ingesta in the small intestine male reproductive tract and a small cyst in the left testicle.

SEPSIS SURGICAL COMPLICATION. This approximately 15-year-old female python was found dead with blood in its cage. It had a history of a coelomic/pulmonary fibrosarcoma that was surgically removed (G99-2606) as well as pneumonia. At necropsy the body was swollen at the site of surgery but sutures were intact. The right eye was large and dark. There was pooled blood at the site of surgery. There was torn small vessel off of the vena cava as the only obvious open vessel. The cranial lung was very congested and there was blood within the lung and trachea. The caudal lung was full of foam. There were small encysted structures within the parenchyma and multiple black areas of black pigment within the serosa. The pericardial sac was filled with fluid. Both ovaries had multiple cystic structures of varying sizes shapes firmness and colors. The gall bladder was very large but easily expressed.

MELANOMA GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This approximately 12-year-old carpet python was donated from Ringling. It had a history of recurrent neoplasia involving the skin. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a mass on the left lateral body wall to 67 cm. from the rostrum that was firm and in the skin and subcutis. The mass was 9 cm. long 7 cm. wide and 4 cm. in depth. A granulomatous or collagenous mass surrounded a firmer layer of necrotic tissue near the ovaries.

PROLIFERATIVE OSTEOARTHROSIS SEMINOMA. This adult python was found dead. It was noted the day prior to death with swelling of the spine and flaccid tail. It died before diagnostics were performed. At necropsy there were moderate coelomic fat bodies. The lungs appeared congested. The heart appeared enlarged. There was bruising of tissues around the heart. The liver appeared grossly enlarged. There were occasional small light tan areas in the parenchyma. There was no food in the upper gastrointestinal tract. The large intestine was distended with a number of fecal boluses. The adrenals appeared enlarged. The majority of the spine was fused. There were areas of osseous proliferation at the bodies of the vertebrae that varied in size and shape. There was a section of spine approximately 12 cm. long that was completely transected from the rest of the spine. The caudal aspect of this fragment had macerated the underlying musculature and into the coelomic cavity. The skin above this area was thin and bruised. The cranial aspect of this fragment had macerated and bruised underlying musculature.

CUTANEOUS MELANOMA WITH VISCERAL METASTASIS. This 17-year-old female green tree python had a history of cutaneous melanoma that was partially excised on two different occasions. The animal died and necropsy revealed swelling just caudal to the old incision site where the melanoma was debulked multifocal white masses in the lung liver and kidney.

EUTHANASIA MESOTHELIOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 5-year-old female ferret was euthanized due to chronic renal disease and abdominal neoplasia. At necropsy a large quantity of milky fluid was present in the abdomen. Numerous small coalescing nodular masses were present on the diaphragm and throughout the mesentery. A mass of material was overlying the pleural surface of the lungs.

SUSPECT NEPHROTOXICITY DUE TO CISPLATIN EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old spayed female black-footed ferret had hepatic carcinoma with surgical removal in the right hepatic lobe. This animal received a regimen of chemotherapy which was stopped due to worsening renal values. The animal was euthanized six months later for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 8-year-old female ferret had a prior diagnosis of lymphoma and was treated with chemotherapeutics for the past six months. The animal’s condition declined acutely approximately four days following the last chemotherapy treatment. The animal was humanely euthanized.

EUTHANASIA PERITONITIS ENTERITIS GASTRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS VACUOLAR DEGENERATION. This 4-year-old male ferret had a history of anorexia weight loss and lethargy. The animal presented acutely with bile peritonitis. Laparotomy revealed enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes and severe peritonitis. Lymph node cytology was consistent with lymphoma and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the anterior mediastinum was expanded by pale pink to tan soft tissue. The abdomen contained 10 ml. of flocculent yellow/tan fluid. The jejunum had a 4 cm. length of thickened wall consisting of firm yellow/white tissue. A pinpoint perforation was identified within the jejunum. The spleen contained a 1 mm. in diameter raised firm white nodule.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS CHRONIC CYSTITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ATELECTASIS INSULINOMA. This 8-year-old female ferret has a recent history of weight loss and stranguria. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy tan to white foci were present in the lungs. Kidneys were irregular and contained fluid filled cysts.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS DERMATOPHYTOSIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 7-year-old male/castrated ferret had a history of chronic adrenal disease and a deslorelin implant placed two months earlier. An insulinoma was managed clinically. The ferret had chronic atelectasis of the cranial segment of the left cranial pulmonary lobe and chronic progressive dermatitis or pyoderma of the face and tail. A resected sebaceous epithelioma of the second digit was also performed in January 2012. The ferret had morbid obesity weakness and may have been immunosuppressed. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.
EUTHANASIA INSULINOMA PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE ENTERITIS. This 6-year-old male ferret has a history of suspected insulinoma. Gross necropsy findings were not provided.
NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS VISCERA. This 3-year-old female/spayed ferret has a history of possible multiple myeloma (G08-5453). Euthanasia was performed and tissues are submitted to check for tumor.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE RENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA HEMANGIOMYELOLIPOMA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This approximately 8-year-old male captive bred ferret has a history of insulinomas and associated therapy followed by diabetes mellitus that required insulin therapy. The ferret was gradually weaned off of insulin but developed cardiopulmonary disease with thoracic effusion. The ferret died and necropsy revealed bloody fluid in the thoracic cavity enlarged heart with pericardial effusion enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes ascites hemorrhagic mass at the root of the mesentery adhesions to the left pancreatic lobe mottled liver enlarged spleen dilated stomach and semifirm masses adjacent to the colon.

EUTHANASIA INSULINOMA SPLENIC MYELOLIPOMA GLOMERULONEPHRITIS. This 5-year-old ferret had a suspected insulinoma. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the distal spleen had a hard raised nodule. A raised red to brown nodule was present in the pancreas.

ISLET CELL VACUOLAR DEGENERATION (POSSIBLE DIABETES MELLITUS) HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 6-year-old female/spayed ferret had a history of periurethral adenocarcinoma islet carcinoma follicular demodicosis and lymphoplasmacytic gastroenteritis. The ferret had recently been listless and had tarry stools. The owner had syringe fed soft food and the ferret regurgitated the food with a small amount of blood. The ferret died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed a pale liver and spleen congested lungs coffee ground colored liquid contents in the stomach and areas of gastric ulceration and an ulcer in the proximal duodenum.

DIABETES MELLITUS ISLET CELL VACUOLAR DEGENERATION PANCREATITIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS ENDOCRINE DERMATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female domestic ferret was diagnosed with insulinoma in 2009 and had been managed with prednisolone since. The ferret also has clinical signs suggestive of adrenal disease but this was not substantiated with blood work. The ferret developed a one week history of lethargy hyperglycemia ketonuria and glucosuria. A midabdominal mass was palpated. Insulin was administered and glucose level returned to level over a two day period. The ferret’s condition subsequently worsened developing diarrhea and partial rectal prolapse and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation fecal staining around the rectum and tail generalized alopecia multiple dark mottled areas on the skin of the legs attributed to hematoma formation associated with venipuncture dark red right caudal and right middle lung lobes moderate periodontal disease digested blood in the stomach trichobezoar in the stomach a 3 cm. mass in the mesentery adjacent to the stomach resembling adipose tissue pale liver large spleen multiple firm round masses in the mesentery adjacent to the jejunum. The right adrenal gland appeared grossly normal and the left adrenal gland could not be located.

NODULAR ACINAR CELL HYPERPLASIA PANCREAS. This 5-year-old male captive bred ferret has a history of insulinoma obese body condition thin haircoat and thin skin possibly due to prednisolone therapy. Surgical palpation of the pancreas revealed two small hard nodules 2 mm. in diameter that were bluntly dissected and submitted.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATITIS NODULAR HEPATOCELLULAR HYPERPLASIA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA LYMPHADENOPATHY ENDOCRINE DERMATOPATHY MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 7-year-old female ferret was euthanized due to a suspected insulinoma and poor quality of life. At necropsy lymph nodes were enlarged and edematous. Kidneys had a finely nodular capsular surface.
HEPATOMA INSULINOMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female ferret has a history of treatment for insulinoma and obesity. The ferret was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA INSULINOMA TRICHOEPITHELIOMA. This 6-year-old polecat was euthanized due to poor body condition. A necropsy a 3 x 4 mm. mass was present in the caudal lobe of the pancreas. Several white nodules were present on the left lung. A 1 cm. proliferative mass was present on the left side of the neck.

EUTHANASIA INSULINOMA LYMPHOID HYPERPLASIA BRONCHOPNEUMONIA HEPATITIS ADRENAL CORTICAL HYPERPLASIA. This 7-year-old male ferret developed seizures and hypoglycemic episodes. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the spleen was markedly enlarged and contained a small soft nodule. A firm mass was present within the pancreas. Small white foci were present in the liver.

ISLET CELL TUMOR INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE FATTY LIVER. This 5-year-old spayed female ferret as humanely euthanized. It had a history of insulinoma that was treated and then became diabetic and then developing normoglycemia.

GASTRIC EROSIONS SEPSIS LOW GRADE INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 5-year-old neutered male ferret had a left adrenalectomy and partial cryotherapy of the right adrenal gland on 4/16/04. In July 04 it was diagnosed with hypoglycemia/possible insulinoma. It was treated with prednisolone twice daily. The ferret subsequently developed a three day history of diarrhea and died. Three other ferrets in the group are affected. Necropsy revealed 2 mm. foci in the lungs possible right atrial enlargement and bloody mucus in the stomach.

EUTHANASIA PANCREATIC INSULINOMA CYSTIC BILIARY HYPERPLASIA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE SPLENIC EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS SUPPURATIVE PANCREATITIS ENTERITIS. This 7-year-old ferret had been treated medically for an insulinoma. Control was no longer possible medically and the animal was euthanized. At necropsy numerous nodules were present in the pancreas and a 1 cm. in diameter nodule was present in the liver.

ISLET AND ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMAS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE WITH FLAGELLATED PROTOZOA CATARACT AND POSSIBLE GLAUCOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old ferret had a history of adrenal disease with deslorelin implant and an insulinoma managed with prednisolone. The ferret also had complete cataracts and was blind. It had a recent history of progressive hair loss and diarrhea. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed severe muscle wasting and potbellied appearance alopecia over the cervical right dorsal and ventral regions and thin remaining coat marked intrathoracic fat congested lungs small amount of intra-abdominal fat reddened gastric mucosa with luminal black mucus hepatomegaly three firm nodules in the pancreas and adhesion to the duodenum red/purple spleen reddening of several mesenteric lymph nodes firm round irregular yellow to red left adrenal gland bilateral cataracts and a 2.5 cm. irregular flat white tissue adhered to the right proximal ribcage.

INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old ferret has a history of inflammatory bowel disease and insulinomas and has recently become diabetic following a second insulinoma surgery. The ferret did poorly despite insulin therapy with associated gastrointestinal upsets and anorexia.

ASTROCYTOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA PANCREATITIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 6.5-year-old neutered male ferret has a history of adrenal disease ataxia and elevated serum enzymes that suggest liver disease and/or inflammatory bowel disease. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a raised focus in the cerebellum that exuded creamy white material on cut surface.

ISLET CELL TUMOR HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS CHOLEMIC NEPHROSIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female/spayed ferret was diagnosed with insulinoma nine months earlier and had been well managed on oral prednisolone. It presented for rapid weight loss despite normal appetite of three weeks duration with elevated hepatic values and hypoglycemia. Supportive care was administered but the animal’s condition continued to decline and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition. The liver was diffusely yellow/tan. A 2 mm. nodule was in the pancreas. The spleen seemed small for the species.

BILATERAL CORTICAL ADENOMAS ISLET CELL ADENOMA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 7-year-old male ferret was previously diagnosed with an insulinoma and two nodules had been removed surgically. The ferret has a two day history of nausea foaming and lethargy with inappetence. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not improve and was found dead in its cage. Necropsy revealed a 2 cm. mass adhered to the fundus of the stomach the lungs were diffusely reddened and some small white smooth areas were in the pulmonary parenchyma increasing in the caudal lobes on the ventral aspect. The right adrenal was 8 mm. in length and had an irregular bumpy appearance. The left adrenal was 1 cm. in length slightly rounder and was filled with white caseous material on cut surface.

ISLET ADENOMAS PANCREATITIS. This 6-year-old male/neutered ferret has been treated six months with prednisolone for insulinoma and has a two month history of hair loss and aggression. During surgery two masses were found in the pancreas. The right adrenal gland was enlarged. The ferret was grossly obese with a large amount of intra-abdominal and subcutaneous fat. The ferret died 36 hours after surgery and had black tarry stools and hypoglycemia prior to death. Necropsy revealed no hemorrhage at the surgical sites yellow liver thickening of the pancreas and white/yellow discoloration of the pancreas and surrounding fat.

CHRONIC GASTROENTERITIS HEPATIC ABSCESS WITH SEPSIS ATYPICAL MYELOID HYPERPLASIA IN BONE MARROW EUTHANASIA. This adult domestic ferret was being treated for chronic adrenal disease (Lupron) and presumptive insulinoma (prednisolone and diazoxide). The patient developed diarrhea shortly after treatment with diazoxide so this was stopped. The patient decompensated quickly after developing the diarrhea and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. It is also noted that this animal had an arrhythmia. Necropsy revealed dark green fluid on the perineum tail and caudal thighs alopecia on the dorsum lateral abdomen and tail bruising at the thoracic inlet and two pinpoint wounds in the intercostal space corresponding to euthanasia injections. Some circular red flat areas were noted in the lungs. There were 15 ml. of opaque serosanguineous fluid noted in the abdominal cavity. Some trichobezoars were noted in the stomach and gastric fluid was opaque and black. Black stringy material was adhered to the mucosal lining of the fundus and a singular circular erosion of the mucosa was noted in the fundus. The liver was diffusely enlarged with yellow reticulated pattern and the cranial surface of the left medial hepatic lobe had a smooth flat 2 x 2 cm. mass elevating the serosa. A multilobulated yellow and red mass 1.5 cm. in greatest dimension was noted on the caudal surface of the right lateral lobe of the lung. The spleen had two well demarcated domed dark red masses elevating the serosa the larger being 2 cm. Adrenal glands could not be located.

INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female/spayed ferret has a history of chronic intermittent diarrhea recent melena and hematochezia and alopecia attributed to adrenal disease. There is also a history of insulinoma. A previous abdominal lymph node aspirate identified suspected lymphoma. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified hemorrhagic abdominal effusion yellow/tan liver with 4 mm. raised red focus on the right lobe a 1 cm. raised red/purple mass on the spleen a right adrenal mass hemorrhagic gastrointestinal contents a 10 cm. flat red/brown structure resembling a parasite in the small intestine and a 6 mm. red/brown mass near the previous pancreatectomy site. Lungs were reddened.

COCCIDIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old male/neutered ferret is from a household in which there are four other ferrets. A new 4-month-old ferret had been introduced but isolated to a different room. Four others lived together. Three of the four had developed inappetence diarrhea bruxism weight loss and dehydration. Supportive care was administered and one with concurrent insulinoma was hospitalized. The ferret of this report received supportive care as above but continued to decline and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed gastric ulcers and petechiae in the serosa of the jejunum and colon.

PULMONARY EDEMA PERIVASCULAR BRONCHIOLAR AND VASCULAR CUFFING BRONCHIECTASIS EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male/neutered ferret has a several year history of insulinoma and heart disease had been diagnosed four months ago. Radiographs revealed pulmonary edema one month ago. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and necropsy revealed reddened lungs that sank in formalin a marked pulmonary and abdominal effusion that was serosanguineous and a 1 cm. in diameter mass in the pancreas. Fewer smaller masses were in the abdomen and the omentum appeared “tangled” and had a small mass at one end.

INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male/neutered ferret was diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease and insulinoma approximately one year earlier and was managed with prednisolone omeprazole and a hypoallergenic diet. Over the past few weeks the ferret’s condition has slowly declined and more recently it developed a recurrent urinary tract infection with bilirubinuria. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed muscle wasting substantial adipose stores in the abdominal cavity small smooth pancreas with a red smooth lesion along the body absence of ingesta from the alimentary tract pale yellow liver and a firm consolidated lesion that extends through the parenchyma of one lobe. The kidneys were surrounded by a large amount of retroperitoneal fat and identification of the adrenal glands was difficult. The adrenals could not be located. A focus of alopecia was on the top of the head. Cataracts were bilateral.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA DILATED LEFT VENTRICULAR CARDIOMYOPATHY COAGULOPATHY RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS. This 7-year-old male/neutered ferret has a one-year history of insulinoma cardiac disease inappetence and hematochezia. The ferret subsequently died and necropsy revealed cardiomegaly possible cranial mediastinal mass congested lungs lobulated liver with several 5 mm. tan foci and several firm green/brown nodules at the base of the lobes multiple 3-4 mm. pancreatic nodules a 1 cm. red/brown firm splenic mass segmental distention of the duodenum and jejunum with red/brown serosal discoloration and multiple trichobezoars in the stomach. At the time of death medications had included prednisolone diazoxide and various cardiac medications.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS PYELONEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS DIABETES MELLITUS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 7-year-old female/spayed ferret has a history of insulinoma and right adrenalectomy. The animal was being managed medically and had recent decline with renal failure urinary tract infection and hyperglycemia with glucosuria. A possible pancreatic mass was identified by ultrasound. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed slightly thin body condition a 6 mm. nodule in the pancreas small kidneys endocrine alopecia enlarged and slightly rounded liver with some 1 mm. white foci.

EUTHANASIA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE ISLET CELL VACUOLATION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 5-year-old female domestic ferret had adrenal disease diagnosed in early 2014 that was treated with deslorelin. An insulinoma was removed in 2014 with resolution of hypoglycemia; however clinical signs of insulinoma returned in 2016. The animal has an approximate two-year history of progressive diarrhea anorexia and weight loss. The animal has been treated supportively with prednisone metronidazole and famotidine. The animal became increasingly lethargic with weight loss and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was an approximately 1 mm. raised mass on the visceral surface of the liver. There were several pinpoint areas throughout the pancreas that were firm.

ISLET CELL TUMORS BLADDER DENERVATION EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male/neutered ferret had a three-year history of enteric disease and a two-year history of heart disease. The ferret also had a 1.5-year history of insulinoma and hind limb weakness with elevated hepatic enzymes. The ferret recently had bladder distention. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA ISLET CELL VACUOLAR DEGENERATION DIABETES MELLITUS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 5-year-old castrated male ferret had a one-month history of lethargy decreased activity level and decreased appetite. The animal had mild hypoglycemia and was treated with insulinoma with no change in clinical signs. The animal subsequently developed coughing sneezing vomiting and diarrhea and died within 24 hours. Necropsy revealed bilateral pulmonary congestion generalized reddening of the small and large intestine some reddening of the pancreas a few small masses in the pancreas moderate hepatic lipidosis moderate renal hyperemia possibly enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes and thin body condition.

INSULINOMAS ADRENAL GLAND CYST REACTIVE LYMPH NODES. This 5-year-old male/neutered ferret has an approximately 4-month history of hypoglycemia starting last September with a glucose of 47. At that time the animal had a slightly elevated globulin of 3.3 a subluxated tail and splenomegaly and was started on diazoxide. In early November 2016 the animal remained hypoglycemic at 50 and the right adrenal gland was palpable. In January left popliteal lymph node was slightly enlarged an oral ulcer was identified behind the incisors and the animal was hypoglycemic at 41. Additionally at this time the animal had slightly increased normal eosinophils at 7%. The animal had exploratory surgery and an approximately 3 mm. pancreatic mass was identified in the right section of the pancreas. The left section of the pancreas had multiple masses that were incised en block with half of the distal aspect of the pancreatic lobe. The right adrenal gland had a cystic nodule and one hard nodule that was dissected out in fragments. Gastrointestinal lymph nodes were slightly enlarged and edematous one of which was biopsied.

EUTHANASIA RENAL GOUT STEATITIS STOMATITIS. This 14-year-old female cobra was diagnosed in May of 2005 with renal adenocarcinoma. Recently the snake became inappetent and less active. Recurrence of the renal mass was identified and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the kidney was effaced by neoplastic tissue.

EUTHANASIA MESOTHELIOMA BILIARY CYSTADENOMA. This 14-year-old male leopard was humanely euthanized due to respiratory distress. At necropsy there was a mass in the thoracic cavity that occupied the entire mediastinum. The lungs were severely atelectatic and congested. There was moderate myocardial congestion. There was thoracic and abdominal serosanguineous effusion.

MESOTHELIOMA ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 12-year-old male clouded leopard had a sudden onset of lethargy inappetence and dyspnea and died while anesthetized for examination. Necropsy revealed a proliferative disease process on the pleural surfaces of the lung and remaining visceral and parietal surfaces of the thoracic cavity. The pleural cavity was filled with slightly cloudy fluid. Some erosions were noted in the stomach and the liver was moderately to markedly enlarged.

MESOTHELIOMA GASTRITIS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 12-year-old female leopard died. It had a history of acute pulmonary distress with inspiratory stridor caused by pleural effusion. At necropsy there was a large tumor within the pleural cavity. There was bloody pleural effusion. The tumor was attached to the left caudal lung lobe. There were smaller metastases on all surfaces of the pleural cavity. There were metastases covering the pericardial sac.

SEMINOMA URATE NEPHROSIS INANITION. This male approximately 10-year/9-month-old guineafowl was found dead in the afternoon. The bird regurgitated that morning and was found to have a doughy consistency mass in the crop that was assumed to be congealed tube feeding formula. The bird also had a two week history of poor doing and had lost weight over the last few months. It had a poor appetite. It had been hospitalized for diagnostics observation and treatment. At necropsy the bird was cachectic. There were green pasty stools around the vent. The spleen was enlarged soft and pale tan. It was irregular on cut section. There were petechiae on the capsular surface. The crop was distended with approximately 35 ml. of thick pasty white ingesta (Emer-Aid). The gall bladder contents were dark green to black and solidified. The cecum contained solid gray/green material.
NA

ATHEROSCLEROSIS AORTIC MINERALIZATION COELOMITIS PULMONARY EDEMA. This 6-year-old male cockatiel was previously diagnosed with osteosarcoma of the ulna. Two years later a mass was noted in the caudoventral coelom. Acute dyspnea developed and the animal died. At necropsy the heart was enlarged. Lungs were consolidated and contained fluid. The liver was pale.

PULMONARY SHOCK PROBABLE AEROSOLIZED TOXIN SEMINOMA HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 25-year-old male cockatiel and its cagemate died unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed firm smooth swelling of the left hard palate millet seed in the choanal slit dark yellow and firm duodenum congested lungs with hemorrhagic fluid and good body condition.

EUTHANASIA INANITION SEMINOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS NEPHROSIS. This adult (approximately 9-year-old) male cockatiel was humanely euthanized. This bird had a history of glucosuria. It was drinking on average between 8-20 ml. of water daily. In late May it fell off its perch and remained recumbent. It was brought to the hospital and propped up in an incubator. Over the next few days his breathing became more labored and he was unable to support himself. At necropsy the bird was in thin body condition. The liver was small and slightly friable. The pancreas was light firm and enlarged.

SEMINOMA SPINAL COLUMN EMACIATION. This 10- to 11-year-old male cockatiel had a six month history of slowly progressive paresis starting on the left and progressing rapidly to the right with a clinical appearance of “curly toe”. A single elevation of bile acid and serum AST was noted in the bird’s history but these return to normal with no nerve deficits. Necropsy revealed an enlarged left kidney with compression of the sciatic nerve.
SEMINOMA. This 20-year-old male captive bred cockatiel had a 3-5 day history of illness and died. Necropsy revealed a mass in the coelomic cavity.

SEMINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old cockatiel has a history of progressive loss of use paresis and paralysis of the legs. Decreased motility of the gastrointestinal tract was also noted. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed megacolon and a mass present that was pressing on the left sciatic nerve and causing the left kidney to bulge.

SEMINOMA. This 12-year-old male captive bred cockatiel had a 1.5 week history of illness and was euthanized for humane reasons. The bird appeared “droopy” and developed respiratory distress. Approximately 10 ml. of fluid was in the abdomen and a large mass was present over the kidneys. A yellow spot was in the right lung.

PULMONARY ABSCESS/ASPIRATION NEPHROSCLEROSIS HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMA THYROID ADENOMA SEMINOMA CHRONIC ABOMASITIS AND ENTEROCOLITIS. This 16-year-old male mountain goat was euthanized due to declining mobility and weakness and poor body condition. Necropsy revealed consolidated cranial left lung with adhesion to the chest wall. Some faint pale streaking was in the myocardium. A 6 cm. encapsulated hepatic mass with a necrotic center was in one lobe. The reticulum contains some foreign material (fabric). The kidneys had a subtle orange peel texture and the left testicle was firmer than the right. Ankylosing spondylosis was in the thoracic spine and osteoarthritis was in multiple joints.

EUTHANASIA GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA HEPATITIS AORTITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS DERMAL FIBROSIS BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA. This 16-year-old male mountain goat had a history of chronic respiratory disease presumed to be atypical mycobacteriosis. Annual TB testing has been negative. Eyelid masses consistent with benign melanomas were previously removed. Recently weight loss has developed. A transtracheal wash was positive for Mycobacterium kansasii. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy 5 mm. in diameter black masses were present on both the left and right eyelids. A 2 cm. chalky mass was present in the abdomen. Granulomas were noted in the abdominal lymph nodes. Lung was dark purple consolidated and contained firm yellow foci. Smaller granulomas were noted in the liver.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS SYSTEMIC LYMPHOCYTIC INFLAMMATION (ENCEPHALITOZOON-LIKE) ERYTHROID CONSUMPTIVE ANOMALY STRESS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female/spayed rabbit has a greater than 14 month history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia. The leukemia responded to prednisolone therapy and did not recur. The animal was subsequently euthanized due to other diseases.

EYELID MELANOMA WITH METASTASIS BILIARY CYST ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 10-year-old male rabbit died while anesthetized for removal of a mass under the right eye. Necropsy revealed scarring on the hocks from previous episodes of “sore hock” a cluster of many cystic structures surrounding the liver and adhered to the lobes blood filled trachea wet lungs that oozed blood on cut surface and no other abnormalities other than a mass on the lower palpebra.

SYSTEMIC ABSCESSES. This approximately 8-year-old male sheep has had a cough for approximately three years. Tracheal culture and sensitivity and blood work in 1998 were within normal limits. The animal was euthanized for humane reasons following radiographic evidence of multiple lung masses. Necropsy revealed masses throughout the lungs spleen pericardial sac liver exudate in the airways serosanguineous fluid in the peritoneum serous fluid in the pericardium white plaques in the epicardium and petechiae on the epicardium thickening of the AV valves osteoarthrosis of the coxofemoral joints and an ulcer on the prepuce. Lung cultures were obtained. Analysis of pericardial fluid revealed a possible mesothelioma based on cytologic evaluation.

EUTHANASIA DENTAL DISEASE (GROSS DIAGNOSIS) HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 12-year-old female sheep had a history of progressive weight loss despite supportive care. The animal also had a melanoma of the right forelimb that was removed several months previously. At necropsy the body was thin but contained adequate fat depots. Several premolars were fractured and purulent material and food were present in the gingiva.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MESENTERIC MINERALIZATION RENAL MINERALIZATION ABOMASITIS INSULINOMA. This 13-year-old female sheep has a history of chronic arthritis and weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining quality of life. At necropsy a firm tan nodule was present in the pancreas. A mineralized pink to tan mass was present in the mesentery.

MESOTHELIOMA (LUNG THORAX) BILIARY CYST HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 18-year-old male lion died under anesthesia. At necropsy several liters of serosanguineous fluid were present in the pleural cavity. Numerous proliferative masses were present on the pleura diaphragm and lungs. The liver contained globular cyst-like masses containing serous fluid. The GI tract was diffusely thickened and firm and contained hemorrhagic and mucoid material.

BRONCHIOLOALVEOLAR ADENOMA MESOTHELIOMA BILIARY CYSTS HEPATITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 28-year-old male lion presented with anorexia lethargy and fever. Treatment was initiated; however the animal’s condition failed to improve. Ultrasound revealed enlargement of the liver with marked cystic changes. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. Multiple large fluid filled cysts replaced extensive portions of the liver. Cystic tissue was also noted in the mediastinum. Firm masses were present on the pleura and within the lung.

ARTHRITIS AND CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SIGNS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) OBESITY DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 22-year-old female African lion had a history of chronic osteoarthritis with progressive hind limb ataxia. The animal developed a possible cerebral episode on 12/6 with transient head tilt and circling. The animal’s condition did not improve and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal had a sebaceous carcinoma removed from the right upper eyelid in June 2014. Necropsy revealed obese body condition unkempt haircoat pulmonary congestion mineralization of the aortic valve cusps and the ascending aorta dark striations on the mucosal surface of the pylorus three large masses in the right hepatic lobe and two smaller masses that were cystic containing dark brown clear fluid. No other abnormalities were noted.

MESOTHELIOMA EUTHANASIA. This 24-year-old female lion was recently euthanized due to declining quality of life and body condition. Necropsy revealed 800 ml. of clear straw-colored fluid and fibrin in the thoracic cavity numerous firm white coalescing plaques on the pericardial surface fibrous adhesions of the apex of the heart and the left ventricle to the pericardium few other fibrous pericardial attachments 30 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the pericardial sac clear cysts on the surface of the left ventricle plaques on the thoracic surface of the diaphragm and on the pleural surfaces of the lungs lymphatic dilatation on the serosal surfaces of the stomach omentum and mesentery and a tortuous common bile duct. Degenerative joint disease was in both stifles the ventral aspect of vertebral body T4 was thickened and had nodular bony proliferation bridging to T5 and T6 and the disk material from T3 through T8 had varying degrees of degeneration with associated narrowing of the intervertebral disk space.

MESOTHELIOMA. This adult female was found dead four days after a physical exam revealed poor body condition. Necropsy revealed coelomic hemorrhage plaque-like areas in the liver and an enlarged uterus containing necrotic material.

POSTSURGICAL DEATH SHOCK. This 9-year/11-month-old female koala went into respiratory arrest postsurgery and was unable to be resuscitated and was euthanized. It had amputation of the right radius and ulna due to osteosarcoma of the distal right radius and ulna. Recovery was slow but appeared uneventful. After extubation it started having episodes of muscle rigidity and excitement. In the PM the animal was evaluated and still appeared weak and disoriented. Nystagmus was present. Hematocrit dropped from 20 to 15% since presurgery. Supplemental oxygen was provided with oxyglobin. The koala had agonal breathing and emergency procedures were started. At necropsy the koala was in good nutritional condition. There was a hematoma present around the amputation site. There was a moderate amount of free blood in the abdominal cavity. The lungs were pale. There was hemorrhage present in the small intestine localized to the jejunum.

DEGENERATIVE VASCULAR RENAL JOINT AND LENTICULAR DISEASE ENDOMETRITIS PANCREATIC ATROPHY RETROVIRUS INFECTION EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old female koala had a history of successful breeding that resulted in multiple nonviable or shortly lived joeys prior to her arrival at Zoo Miami in 2007. The koala was suspected to be in early stages of retroviral-induced leukemia/lymphoma in 2009. The animal was in thin body condition so supplemental nutrition was offered daily in addition to supportive care that included anti-inflammatory drugs for osteoarthritis. In 2013 the koala developed intermittent periods of inappetence weight loss and low fecal output. Supportive care was administered during these episodes. In April 2015 an antiviral drug was administered for two months but the koala became leukopenic so the medication was discontinued. The koala failed to respond to supportive treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fair body condition light yellow colored ridge within the tracheal lumen congested right lung a 2 cm. region of white discoloration along the cranial aspect of the right lung roughened texture to the epicardial surface of the right ventricle proliferative tricuspid valve that was granular and thickened white nonraised foci on the serosal surface of the kidneys a focus of dark discoloration in the right renal medulla and a darkened area around the left renal pelvis. The adrenal glands were small. An ectopic spleen was identified. The right acetabulum was rough and erosion was present along both femoral heads. White semitransparent fluid was within the uterus. Klebsiella pneumoniae was cultured from the fluid in the uterus. A eucalyptus gruel was in the stomach and the pylorus was thickened.

EUTHANASIA ATHEROSCLEROSIS SEMINOMA HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS TRACHEITIS AIR SACCULITIS PORTAL HEPATITIS. This 32-year-old male flamingo was humanely euthanized. It had a history of ataxia and was unable to stand or walk normally. At necropsy the left testis was 5 x 4.5 cm. The liver was dark brown and friable. The aorta was thickened and irregular near the kidneys.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA MYOSITIS CONJUNCTIVITIS. This male greater than 20-year-old flamingo was humanely euthanized. It had a history of corneal rupture and enucleation. Lacrimal gland adenocarcinoma was found. Radiation treatment was done at TUSVM for four weeks. The flamingo was returned to the zoo and integrated back into the flock. It was keeping good weight but was somewhat aloof from the flock. It seemed a little disoriented from time to time. It had a high titer to West Nile virus during screening in the summer. It was found acutely sternal on exhibit. It appeared weak and could not hold its head up. It had decreased mentation. It was treated with supportive care. The flamingo remained recumbent and was not eating. There was no change in its status. At necropsy there was severe bruising on the lower one-third of the neck. There was muscle tissue hemorrhage that was edematous and purple-green. There was possible luxation of the cervical vertebrae. The pancreas had several pinpoint red foci on the surface.

UROLITHIASIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SWIM BLADDER MINERALIZATION RENAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS SEROSAL GRANULOMA BILATERAL SEMINOMAS EUTHANASIA. This adult male seadragon had progressive inappetence and finally anorexia of one day’s duration was found weak and lying at the bottom of the exhibit with a large wound on the ventral snout and a skin erosion on the entire finlet of the left side of the cloaca. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed many 1-2 mm. white encysted nodules along the serosa of the intestine scant adipose that was discolored yellow/gold two irregular tan/white bladder stones up to 0.5 cm. in greatest dimension and no other gross abnormalities. A wet amount of the finlet skin erosion revealed many elongated ciliated protozoa and bacteria.

HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS WITH MELANOMACROPHAGE HYPERPLASIA. This 8-year-old frog was found dead with no previous abnormalities noted. Gross necropsy revealed a single 2 x 1.5 cm. urinary calculus within the bladder. No other abnormalities were found.

BACTERIAL TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS ASCITES MELANOMA CHOLELITHIASIS. This 8-year-old female toad presented with bloat and was spending an unusual amount of time at the surface of the tank. The toad subsequently died and necropsy revealed moderate ascites a 5 mm. raised soft tissue nodule on the right dorsal forelimb consolidated lungs that sank in formalin rounded hepatic margins a lobe-like appendage to the gallbladder with firm bile-stained material in the center three rocks in the pyloric region of the stomach a thin-walled dilated sac distal to the stomach containing luminal brown fluid empty urinary bladder mild follicular development and a cone-shaped structure in the oviduct. Adipose stores were atrophic.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE PANCREATIC FIBROSIS IRIS MELANOMA ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 5-year-old male rock hyrax was sedated for blood collection recovered well in its crate but then developed an abnormal respiratory pattern and hiccups. The animal then arrested twice in which case resuscitation efforts were successful the first time but not the second time. This animal had a deslorelin implant for aggression control. Necropsy revealed adequate adipose stores marked atrophy of the testes shrunken spleen and no other abnormalities.

SEPSIS IRON STORAGE DISEASE CHRONIC CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE (POSSIBLY DIABETIC). This 4-year-old female/spayed rock hyrax has a history of pyometra and uterine sarcoma diagnosed a few weeks earlier. The animal subsequently died and necropsy revealed enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes few white nodules in the liver and swollen kidneys with adhered capsule. The previously excised uterus was filled with thick yellow purulent material with thickened firm walls.

EUTHANASIA SEMINOMA SEPSIS. This adult male lungfish was humanely euthanized. It presented 2.5 weeks prior to euthanasia for a bulge in the abdomen that was demarcated by a small area of pink skin caudal to the vent at the right pelvic fin. The abdomen was aspirated and cloudy light brown fluid was recovered. Similar fluid was released when the pink area was biopsied. Cytology suggested neoplasia or severe inflammatory disease. Antibiotics were started pending a curator’s decision. The animal declined in health over the next two days. At necropsy the fish appeared to have adequate body muscling but no normal fat deposits. Both brille were clouded. The skin that contained the orange/pink discoloration was located directly caudal to the right pelvic fin. There were two other areas of pink discoloration (3 mm. in diameter) noted on the right lateral side between the pelvic and pectoral fins. A third area of skin was ulcerated in the same location. Additional fluid was released when samples were collected from the caudal most lesion. The abnormal skin coincided with masses found intracoelomically. The masses were complex and multilobed. On cut section they seemed fatty but denser in consistency. The largest mass was 7 cm. in diameter located in the right coelom directly caudal to the liver. The liver seemed similarly hardened and potentially attached to the masses. On cut section portions of the liver contain the same material found in the masses. The lungs were moist and congested. The gastrointestinal tract contained substantial contents in the caudal tract.

GRANULOMATOUS ENTERITIS AND PNEUMONIA PERFORATED CROP DYSGERMINOMA SEPSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS WITH DISSECTING ANEURYSM. This 26-year-old female parakeet had a history of inability to fly due to a previous wing fracture but could navigate the enclosure well. The bird had been treated one month earlier for Sarcocystis neurona after an enclosure mate died due to sarcocystosis. At the time of treatment the bird had a markedly elevated white blood cell count and elevated bile acids remained clinically stable through treatment and was released back into the aviary. The bird presented one month later after falling from a perch and examination revealed weakness and thin body condition. Supportive care was administered but the bird developed neurologic signs and died several hours later. Necropsy revealed emaciation emphysema under the skin over the keel absence of adipose tissue white and red discoloration in the lungs a small amount of fluid in the trachea mottled areas of tan discoloration in the liver.

PORVENTRICULAR DILATATION DISEASE CUTANEOUS MELANOMA. This female approximately 10-year-old parrot was found dead. The bird had a history of wanting to be fed by its mate. The bird had not been closely monitored. Necropsy revealed dark purple lungs and food throughout the gastrointestinal tract.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE DEGENEARATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE RENOLITH. This 18.5-year-old male Rodriguez flying fox had a digit amputation in June 2015 with a diagnosis of spindle cell sarcoma and complete excision (G15-3179). The patient was clinically normal and was found unable to use its hind limbs the day of death. Radiographs revealed lysis of the pelvis and proximal femurs bilaterally and destruction of both hip joints. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the liver had multifocal white pinpoint nodules. The kidneys were subjectively pale and enlarged.

SHOCK RENAL TUBULAR PIGMENT DEPOSITION. This subadult (approximately 16- to 18-month-old) female 82 lb. cougar was captured in excellent condition in January 2006. Mortality signal was received and the cougar was recovered in early April 2006 and appeared to have been dead 2-3 days. The cougar was found in Riparian Habitat less than one meter from a creek. No clear signs of trauma were noted and there was some evidence of weight loss. The remains of a domestic cat recently eaten were found 8-10 meters from the cougar. The weight of the cougar at necropsy was 67 lbs. and necropsy revealed low to moderate fat reserves. Water-like blood was collected from the heart and body cavity and stored in a refrigerator in red and lavender top vials. The movements and behaviors of this cougar were normal up until the time of mortality. This cougar is the offspring of a cougar that was confirmed to have died due to complications of feline leukemia virus infection in August 2006. Telemetry data suggested that they were a functional family group up until one week before mortality.

EPICARDIAL HEMORRHAGE AUTOLYZED TISSUE. This 2.5-year-old male Florida panther was found dead. Thoracic blood tested positive for feline leukemia virus. The carcass was autolyzed and had been frozen prior to necropsy. The cause of death was not determined.
ASTROCYTOMA PULMONARY EDEMA. This 1-year-old rat was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy lungs were nearly completely effaced by consolidation and inspissated material.

EUTHANASIA (PROBABLE INSULINOMA). This approximately 2-year-old intact male rat had a one day history of seizures associated with profound hypoglycemia elevated hepatic values and bilirubinuria. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and a 6 mm. red irregular round mass was noted at the tip of the splenic limb of the pancreas.

BRAIN TUMOR (PROBABLE ASTROCYTOMA). This 1-year-old female/spayed captive bred domestic rat has an approximately two week history of severe weight loss with circling to the left. No abnormalities were known on physical examination. A brain lesion was suspected and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA ASTROCYTOMA. This 2-year-old male rat had a history of seizures and was euthanized. At gross necropsy the left cerebrum was discolored and a small 1-2 mm. mass was located just rostral to the cerebellum on the dorsal midline.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ASTROCYTOMA EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male rat has a three month history of respiratory tract disease and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed diffusely hemorrhagic pulmonary fields and an enlarged liver. The liver and kidney were reddened.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA WITH OTITIS MEDIA INTRATHORACIC NEOPLASM (BRONCHOGENIC OR MESOTHELIOMA). This greater than 2-year-old male domestic rat was found dead. Necropsy revealed a thick caseating infiltrate in the lungs congested meninges and no other abnormalities. This animal periodically had nose bleeds head tilt and a long history of respiratory problems. Head tilt was severe one day prior to death.

LYMPHOCYTIC DERMATITIS AND DERMAL VASCULITIS VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male Egyptian fruit bat had a few week history of ulcerative ventral cervical dermatitis that responded moderately but transiently to conservative topical treatment. Biopsies identified an atypical lymphoid infiltrate suggestive of lymphoma and the bat was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fair nutritional condition moderate dehydration and a 3.5 cm. area of alopecia with ulceration and thickened skin overlying the ventral mandible and ventral cervical region.

SEVERE INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS AND GLOMERULONEPHRITIS POSSIBLE LEPTOSPIROSIS PERITONITIS. This 12-year-old female mustache tamarin was found dead in its enclosure. It had a recent history of abdominal distention dyspnea hepatomegaly and jaundice. It had a recent tail amputation surgery and liver and skin biopsy in conjunction with an ovariohysterectomy. A adenocarcinoma (G99-0097) was noted histologically. Recent clinical pathologic data included hypoproteinemia uremia increased creatinine and monocytosis. At necropsy the thoracic cavity contained approximately 5 ml. of pink clear fluid. There were small yellow nodules on the atrioventricular valve. There was approximately 5 ml. of straw pink fluid within the abdominal cavity. There was no digesta present within the stomach. The descending colon was adhered to the urinary bladder and left abdominal wall. The liver was large congested firm and had rounded edges. The spleen was contracted. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. The urinary bladder was adhered to the descending colon and vagina. The kidneys had irregular small cysts in the cortex. The gall bladder was thickened and irregular with adhesions to the body wall.

POSTOPERATIVE SEPSIS COLON REPRODUCTIVE TRACT INCISION SITE. This greater than 10-year-old female tree boa has a previous history of intestinal resection and anastomosis due to adenocarcinoma (G08-0532). Three weeks after surgery the surgical skin wound was noted to be dehiscing and the patient was taken to surgery again for exploration. Surgery revealed apparent infection in the coelomic cavity and severe necrosis of the large intestine anterior and posterior to the anastomosis site. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS BARBITURATE ARTIFACT. This greater than 8-year-old male blue spiny lizard had been eating well the past three months. It developed a three week episode of decreased appetite and lethargy became obtunded and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition dull skin with urates adhered to the vent dilated cecum filled with thick brown material full gallbladder dark liver with few tan spots on the edges and hyperpigmentation of the body wall and one kidney. This group of lizards has a history of lymphoma.

MELANOMA COELOMIC VISCERA SOURCE UNDETERMINED; IMPACTED UROPYGIAL GLAND. This 28-year-old male wild caught penguin died spontaneously and was refrigerated six hours prior to necropsy. The animal had been found dead. Necropsy revealed a greatly enlarged black and gray liver congested lungs with palpable nodules and an enlarged heart.

HEPATIC MELANOMA SYSTEMIC NONSUPPURATIVE INFLAMMATION EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male Humboldt penguin has a history of weight loss and regurgitation with a firm irregular soft tissue mass and elevated hepatic enzymes. Exploratory laparotomy revealed a nonresectable cystic hepatic mass affecting multiple hepatic lobes and associated with severe compression of the stomach and intestines and the bird was subsequently euthanized. Necropsy revealed a hyperkeratotic mass in the inner inguinal area bilaterally two 2 cm. in diameter black masses in the right lung lobe one 1 cm. black mass in the left lung lobe and multiple coalescing black masses throughout the liver. A 4 cm. white mass was in the area of the gall bladder.

ENDOCARDIOSIS ADRENAL CORTICAL CARCINOMA COLONIC CARCINOMA IN SITU CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE HEPATIC NODULAR HYPERPLASIA. This 16-year-old female potbelly pig was euthanized due to hyporexia weight loss lethargy and a recent seizure-like episode. Additionally the animal had a systolic heart murmur. At necropsy multiple masses were identified including papillomatous masses extending from the colonic mucosa masses associated with the right adrenal gland and enlarged pituitary.

CHRONIC COELOMITIS. This 8-year-old male pheasant had been acting normally one day prior to death and was subsequently found dead in the morning. It had no prior signs of illness. The animal had been in the same area as a few birds with some unusual bleeding issues. One of these birds had aspergillosis. A golden pheasant from this group had vascular necrosis with hemorrhage and aspergillosis (G12-5890) and a Lady Amherst’s pheasant had Heterakis infection zygomycosis and a renal tubular adenocarcinoma (G12-5897). Necropsy for the bird of this report identified clear slightly yellow mucoid material on the serosal surfaces of the viscera. The liver was reddened. The intestine was congested and the serosa was hemorrhagic. Hemorrhage was also present on the mucosal surface of the proventriculus. The spleen was reddened and the vessels of the heart were injected. A few pale areas were in the heart. The lungs were severely hemorrhagic on cut surface.

SEMINOMA URATE STASIS HEPATITIS. This 10-year-old male tanager presented with dyspnea and abdominal distention. A surgical exploratory was attempted but the bird died under anesthesia. At necropsy a large irregular tan mass was present adherent to the liver and GI tract.

OSTEOARTHRITIS CUTANEOUS MELANOMA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 40-year-old male South American tapir had a history of chronic arthritis and melanoma. The melanoma had appeared to resolve grossly after treatment with cryotherapy. The tapir was found dead in its exhibit. Necropsy revealed osteoarthritic lesions in the coxofemoral joints sand in the stomach and hard plastic foreign bodies in the cecum.

EUTHANASIA NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This approximately 18-year-old captive bred male Russian tortoise was euthanized. The tortoise had been rescued in August 2013 from a home with terrible husbandry. The tortoise had hind limb paraparesis and constipation that never improved. Necropsy revealed possible disseminated melanomacrophage staining in the liver and a dilated large intestine with subjectively thin walls.
GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR MELANOMA BACTERIAL COELOMITIS AND SEPTICEMIA. This 9-year-old female wild caught garter snake was submitted with no additional history (necropsy report to follow).

SEMINOMA POSSIBLE HERMAPHRODITE. This 21-year-old eastern blue-tongued skink has a history of gingivitis and was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed a large mass in the coelomic cavity occupying approximately 80% of the coelomic space. Pulmonary lobes were collapsed and compressed cranially. The liver was dark green and compressed cranially against the coelomic wall. The pylorus and duodenum felt firm and thickened. Three to four focal discrete slightly raised white nodular structures were in the mesentery. The mass appeared to arise from the reproductive tract and was cystic containing approximately 90 ml. of clear yellow proteinaceous fluid. Several smaller structures were present on the surface of the mass and also filled with fluid. The inner surface of the mass was white with thickened areas and occasionally irregular raised small white bumps.

OVARIAN DYSGERMINOMA XANTHOMATOSIS INANITION. This 14-year-old skink had a history of weight loss. Recent fecal exams were positive for yeast and oxyurids. The animal was under treatment but was found dead. At necropsy the skink was thin with marked muscle wasting and no observable fat depots. A large quantity of straw colored fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. Numerous white masses were present on the serosal surface of several organs. A cluster of cystic masses was present in the mid coelom surrounded by firm yellow material.

EUTHANASIA SEMINOMA MICROSPOIRDIAN COLITIS RENAL CYSTADENOMA RENAL GOUT. This approximately 26-year-old male skink was humanely euthanized. The skink had a history of decreased appetite. At necropsy there were significant accumulations of fat in the caudal aspects of the body cavity. The bladder had accumulations of yellow/gold to greenish debris. The bladder wall thickness seemed normal. There was a moderate amount (approximately 15 cc.) of fluid in the body cavity. The heart appeared larger than expected. One of the atrial chambers seemed to have a large scar tissue infarct area. The kidneys were smaller than expected and irregular in their surface texture. On section there were fine whitish nodules throughout. Near the area of thyroid there appeared to be a 0.7 cm. round mass.

DEGENERATIVE SPINAL CORD LESIONS EUTHANASIA. This 25-year-old male bear had a several month history of hind leg lameness and occasional weakness with sudden onset of hind leg paresis three weeks earlier. It showed initial improvement but remained unable to stay standing and tended to crawl on its knees and drag its legs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed moderate overweight body condition minor abrasions and scabbing over the cranial stifle joints linear scar with crusting over the mid back from a site of previous squamous cell carcinoma worn teeth symmetrical homogeneous but large thyroids globoid heart with some dilatation of the right ventricle gray discoloration of the entire heart irregularity of the mitral valve leaflets pitted intimal surfaces of the aorta and pulmonary artery rounding of the right lobe of the liver ingesta in the stomach and intestines thick walled pylorus gritty texture to the adrenals on cut surface possible mild narrowing of the spinal canal and compression over the caudal cord at L5-L6 and narrowing of the disk space at L6-L7 but no evidence of disk protrusion.

SEMINOMA PARABRONCHITIS URATE STASIS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This 3-year-old male lorikeet was found dead. Necropsy revealed a contusion on the skull and in the muscle near the left leg good body condition slightly enlarged liver empty alimentary tract and a markedly enlarged left testicle with adhesion to the kidney.

SEMINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male tree shrew had a history of enlargement of the right scrotum and the right testicle was removed surgically. The animal did not recover well from anesthesia and was euthanized.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS CHRONIC CYSTITIS MYCOTIC RHINITIS PNEUMONIA DYSGERMINOMA (OVARY) GASTRIC MINERALIZAITON MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 17-year-old female snow leopard had a history of chronic renal disease and hematuria. No response was seen with treatment and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the ribs were noted to be soft and pliable. The left ovary was markedly enlarged and contained hemorrhagic fluid. Granular white material was present in the urinary bladder. The stomach contained multiple small firm nodular masses. An abscess was identified in the lung. A black to green mass containing purulent material was present in the left nasal sinus. Dark discoloration was noted over the cerebrum and cerebellum.

MESOTHELIOMA SARCOCYSTIS CYST (HEART) EUTHANASIA. This approximately 20-year-old male Kodiak bear developed a sudden onset of dyspnea associated with a hemorrhagic pleural effusion. The animal was humanely euthanized and necropsy revealed a hemorrhagic pleural effusion grape-like clusters of masses involving the outside of the entire mediastinum on both sides of the chest with no involvement of the lungs mild arthritis.

VERTEBRAL DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA EMACIATION EPICARDIAL MELANOMA. This 14-year-old male crocodile monitor was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes secondary to marked vertebral fusion and bony proliferation. At necropsy there were several firm nodules on the skin. The heart had thickening of the atrioventricular valves. There was marked bony proliferation throughout the spine.

ASTROCYTOMA EUTHANASIA. This greater than 10-year-old male white winged dove was euthanized following a one month history of ocular discharge and irritation within the right eye. The eye responded initially to antibiotics but then the discharge returned. The bird then developed a right-sided head tilt and stopped eating several days priori to euthanasia. At necropsy the bird was in body condition. The left side of the cranium appeared slightly larger than the right. The right eyelid margin appeared irregular and there was periocular feather loss. There was a small healed defect in the skull between and just above the eye level. The liver appears slightly mottled. All other systems were grossly unremarkable. Samples of heart lung liver and muscle were frozen for future use if needed.

OOPHORITIS OVARIAN DYSGERMINOMA. This 12-year-old morning dove was found openmouthed breathing. An attempt was made to place an air sac tube; however on entering the coelom yellow fluid emerged and the animal died. At necropsy dark yellow fluid was present throughout the coelom. The heart was enlarged.
